categories.name: Prompt Injection & Agent Security Research
categories.summary: A significant cluster of research papers and tools focused on prompt injection vulnerabilities in LLM agents emerged today. Key themes include indirect prompt injection via web browsing proxies, clarification-seeking behavior amplifying attack surfaces, and contextual integrity as an evaluation framework. The research collectively highlights that traditional data-vs-instruction separation is insufficient for securing agentic systems.

key_items.title: IPI-proxy: Red-teaming web-browsing agents via intercepting proxy
key_items.detail: An intercepting proxy that rewrites HTTP responses to embed hidden instruction payloads, enabling realistic prompt injection testing on production-like browsing flows rather than static benchmarks.

key_items.title: ASPI: Clarification requests amplify prompt injection vulnerability
key_items.detail: Research demonstrating that prompt injection success rates increase significantly when agents solicit clarification from users, establishing clarification channels as distinct trust boundaries requiring gating.

key_items.title: Contextual Integrity framework for evaluating agent injection failures
key_items.detail: Paper arguing that attackers can craft context to make blocked information flows appear norm-compliant, proposing Contextual Integrity as a lens for context-sensitive agent security evaluation.

key_items.title: LLM Threats Analysis: Checklist-style threat model for injection vectors
key_items.detail: A practical threat model covering where untrusted instructions cross trust boundaries in LLM apps and MCP tool flows, helping teams place controls outside the model.

categories.name: Security Tools & Detection Systems
categories.summary: Several new security tools were released targeting MCP tool poisoning detection and prompt injection simulation. These tools enable security teams to implement pre-invocation guardrails and conduct hands-on testing of injection scenarios before deploying agents with elevated privileges.

key_items.title: MCP Prompt Injection Detector with explainable ML
key_items.detail: Hybrid embeddings + XGBoost system for pre-invocation detection of tool-poisoning or prompt-injection content in MCP tool calls, providing explainable guardrail signals.

key_items.title: PromptForage: Interactive LLM prompt injection security lab
key_items.detail: A hands-on testing environment for exercising prompt injection scenarios in controlled settings, useful for documenting injection patterns before granting tool or data-access privileges.

categories.name: Agent Supply Chain & Credential Security
categories.summary: Research and industry solutions emerged addressing agent supply chain attacks and credential management. A notable paper demonstrated payload-less skill attacks that evade signature scanners, while credential brokering solutions aim to reduce prompt injection blast radius by keeping secrets out of model context.

key_items.title: Payload-less skills exploit LLM agent supply chains
key_items.detail: Research showing that benign-looking skills can steer agents via natural-language compliance rules, causing harmful action synthesis at runtime—highlighting the need to evaluate skills by intent, not just static payload detection.

key_items.title: Credential brokering architecture for AI agents explained
key_items.detail: Architectural pattern that reduces prompt injection blast radius by brokering short-lived, policy-scoped access at tool boundaries rather than including long-lived secrets in model context.

key_items.title: Proton Pass adds monitored credential sharing for AI agents
key_items.detail: New feature providing scoped tokens for selected vault items with activity visibility, offering narrower delegation paths than full credential handover for agent use cases.

categories.name: Vulnerability Disclosures & CVEs
categories.summary: Two notable CVEs affecting AI tooling were disclosed: a PydanticAI SSRF bypass via IPv4-mapped IPv6 encoding, and a Kiro CLI authorization bypass through piped stdin. Both highlight the brittleness of blocklist-only defenses and the importance of treating non-interactive inputs as untrusted in CLI agent contexts.

key_items.title: CVE-2026-46678: PydanticAI SSRF cloud-metadata blocklist bypass
key_items.detail: IPv4-mapped IPv6 encoding bypasses cloud-metadata IP blocklist when forcedownload='allow-local' is enabled—an incomplete fix of CVE-2026-25580. Reinforces need for network-boundary egress enforcement.

key_items.title: CVE-2026-9255: Kiro CLI tool execution without authorization via stdin
key_items.detail: Missing input-source validation allows piped stdin to bypass authorization prompts, enabling tool execution including shell commands without user approval in the AWS Kiro CLI.

categories.name: AI-Powered Vulnerability Discovery
categories.summary: Anthropic's Project Glasswing update revealed that Claude Mythos Preview has discovered over 10,000 high/critical vulnerabilities in essential software within one month, prompting recommendations for shortened patch cycles. This signals a potential acceleration in the vulnerability discovery landscape driven by frontier AI models.

key_items.title: Anthropic Glasswing update: Claude Mythos finds 10,000+ critical vulnerabilities
key_items.detail: One-month update on Project Glasswing reveals the unreleased Claude Mythos Preview model has helped partners uncover thousands of high-severity vulnerabilities, with Anthropic advising developers to shorten patch cycles.

key_items.title: Anthropic Glasswing initial research update
key_items.detail: Official Anthropic research post on the Glasswing project's initial findings and methodology for AI-assisted vulnerability discovery.

key_items.title: CERT.PL: Autonomous fuzzing techniques
key_items.detail: Technical post from CERT Poland on autonomous fuzzing approaches, complementing the AI-driven vulnerability discovery trend.

top_insights: Prompt injection research is maturing beyond simple injection-detection toward understanding contextual and behavioral amplifiers—clarification-seeking behavior and contextual manipulation now recognized as distinct attack surfaces requiring dedicated controls.
The MCP (Model Context Protocol) ecosystem is receiving focused security tooling attention, with multiple detection and threat analysis tools released specifically for MCP tool poisoning scenarios.

Agent supply chain security is emerging as a critical concern, with research demonstrating that payload-less, natural-language compliance rules can weaponize ostensibly benign skills without triggering traditional signature-based detection.

AI-powered vulnerability discovery is entering production scale—Anthropic's 10,000+ vulnerability findings in one month signals that organizations may need to fundamentally reassess patch cycle timelines.

Defense-in-depth for AI agents increasingly requires architectural controls (credential brokering, network-boundary enforcement, tool-call policy) rather than relying on prompt-level or blocklist-based mitigations alone.
